stances_toward.note: Albania has adopted all EU Council decisions on Russia into domestic law since 2014 (decision 597/2025 lists over 2,500 persons and entities), turned back 207 Russian nationals at the border between 2022 and April 2026 and blocks RT and Sputnik; BIRN's July 2026 audit found almost no enforcement cases and calls trade and financial ties 'very limited' and relations cool for decades. Russia has no leverage on Tirana and does not recognise Kosovo, which Albania treats as kin. Rival, not adversary: Albania does not seek Moscow's defeat. Our reading of the structure (confidence C).

stances_toward.note: Russia supports the entity, not the state: Dodik met Putin in Moscow on 9 May 2026 with RS premier Minic and president Karan, Moscow calls the OHR 'incompatible with the sovereignty of [BiH]' and does not recognise Schmidt, and Dodik thanked Putin, who had declared his support, after the SNSD victory of 4 Oct 2026 (BIRN). Yet Russia voted for the EUFOR renewal in Oct 2025 (15-0) and the 29 Dec 2025 presidential statement. Sarajevo has not imposed sanctions on Russia because RS blocks it (Dodik's claim). Not 'adversary': Russia neither threatens the state's existence nor seeks its end, and the Bosniak-led side keeps the Council channel open. No source uses a scale word (confidence C). Bond grievance: Russia's support for Serbs and its veto-threats on the OHR. 'Since' is the contested 2021 appointment of Schmidt.

stances_toward.note: No source calls the relationship 'rival'; the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C). Croatia applies the EU sanctions on Russia, refused in Feb 2026 to let Russian Druzhba crude pass through JANAF to Hungary and Slovakia, supplies Ukraine with arms (over EUR 300m since 2022) and is replacing Russian gas with Krk LNG. Not 'adversary': Zagreb does not seek Russia's collapse, and trade continues at a small scale (goods imports from Russia EUR 174m in 2025, 0.4%). Russia is Serbia's patron, which adds a Balkan layer to the grade. Bond none.

stances_toward.note: Skopje expelled five Russian diplomats on 28 Mar 2022 and six more in April, for activities contrary to the Vienna Convention, and applies every EU restrictive measure on Russia and Belarus (the Commission: 'full alignment'). Moscow called the allegations unfounded and warned of consequences; disinformation researchers in Skopje document Russian narratives around the 2018 name referendum and the Sofia-Skopje dispute. Rival, not adversary: Skopje wants no confrontation beyond NATO and EU alignment, and the Mickoski government has been quiet. Confidence C because no source in the pool uses 'rival' and nothing recent (2025-26) was found; an alleged Russian influence on the 2024 vote is not sourced. Bond - grievance: Moscow's role against the name deal and its patronage of Serbia's positions.

stances_toward.note: Montenegro has applied EU sanctions since March 2022, expelled six Russian diplomats on 29 Sep 2022 (Russia then suspended consular services), pledged in November 2025 to tighten visas for Russians, and on 9 Oct 2026 arrested and expelled the founder of the Rybar network with four associates on national-security grounds. The European Parliament (June 2026) names third-country interference and disinformation against Montenegro's EU and NATO course. Not 'adversary': Russia was the first Security Council member to recognise Montenegro in 2006, Russians are 16.4% of foreign overnights (2025) and the state seeks no regime change in Moscow. Bond - grievance: the 2016 coup plot (2019 verdict; 2024 retrial acquitted all defendants, so the judicial record is contested) and Moscow's opposition to NATO accession.

relations_to.summary: Bosnia takes all its natural gas from Russia, delivered through Serbia via TurkStream and a single 1979 pipeline (up to about 8% of its energy use). The Southern Interconnection with Croatia is the planned alternative; the US State Department warned Sarajevo in June 2026 against delay after RS officials met Gazprom.

relations_to.summary: A Republika Srpska delegation - Dodik, president Karan, Speaker Stevandic, later premier Minic - went to Moscow for Victory Day on 9 May 2026 and met Putin; Dodik called the relationship strategic and said RS prevents Bosnia from imposing sanctions on Russia. An entity delegation, not a state one; the state-level foreign ministry plays no part.
relations_to.note: Dodik's claims about blocking sanctions are his own assertions and are not verified. Most coverage is from RS-friendly Serbian media; the independent account of the Kremlin meeting is missing.
